# Perform Engle's ARCH LM test

<small>Source: [`man/performArchLMTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performArchLMTest.Rd) · Help: `?performArchLMTest`</small>

Regresses squared residuals on their lags to detect ARCH effects.

## Usage

```r
performArchLMTest(model, data = NULL, lags = 1)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   optional data frame the model was fitted to. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. The statistic is computed from the residuals of `model`, so `data` does not change the result; it is accepted so that every test takes `(model, data, ...)`. Before 0.15.0 the second argument was `lags`: a number passed there by position is still read as `lags`, with a warning that shows the new call; that form stops working in 1.0.0.

`lags`
:   number of lags to include.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the test statistic, p-value and degrees of freedom.

## Details

The statistic is \(n R^2\) from an auxiliary regression of \(e_t^2\) on its lagged values, where \(R^2\) is the coefficient of determination. Under the null of no ARCH effects it follows a chi-square distribution with degrees of freedom equal to the number of lags.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Since 0.16.0 it is built on the model context, and also refuses
a multivariate `lm` ("needs a model with one response"), a fit whose coefficients, residuals or
weights were changed after the fit, and a fit with `model = FALSE` whose model frame, rebuilt
from the data it was fitted to, no longer holds its response, because those data changed after the
fit, with or without `data`. A fit with `model = FALSE` whose data are gone is tested on
`data` that give its response and fitted values, and refused without them. The test reads
nothing from `data`, which is checked as before: it must hold the variables of the model and
the row names of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Engle, R. F. (1982). Autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity with estimates of the variance of United Kingdom inflation. *Econometrica*, 50(4), 987–1007. [doi:10.2307/1912773](https://doi.org/10.2307/1912773)

Hamilton, J. D. (1994). *Time Series Analysis*. Princeton University Press.

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 performArchLMTest(m, lags = 2)
```
